en: "But there should be a Pyroglyph researcher among the goblins of Baroque Fort."{w}
"You're right, there was! An old goblin geezer like that!"{w}
"Why not try asking them?"{w}
note: Rondelgius suggests asking the goblins ([JP]); addressed to Haleorat and the party.

en: "Good thinking!{w}Sorry, but could you guys go to Baroque Fort and get this score deciphered for us?"{w}
note: [JP] = casual 'sorry (to ask)'. [JP]: the party is to get it read, via the goblin researcher just mentioned.

en: "I am rather curious myself. I would very much ask it of you."{w}
"Hey there, want to stick around and hear a song?"{w}
"How far have you gotten with deciphering the score?{w}If you figure it all out, be sure to let us in on it too!"{w}

"You deciphered it? The writing on the score!?{w}So this song is called Urnade...
Let me play it right away."{w}
note: Urnade per glossary (song title, no brackets in source).

en:
Urna wished for a little happiness
Breathing in the earth, the first friend{w}{p}Hand in hand, let us celebrate the two who met
Fingertips touching, the warmth of the soil{w}{p}Urna wished for an endless sky
Dance through the heavens, the second friend{w}{p}The wind blows through, binding heaven and earth
Hold it close, and feel a beloved life{w}{p}Urna wished for a fire in the heart
Burn, O soul, the third friend{w}{p}Dwelling in the breast, a hymn to life
And here abides a hope that never dies{w}{p}Urna wished for peaceful water
Drifting in the deep, the fourth friend{w}{p}Shining on a sleeping face, the waves of moonlight
O happiness, may you last forever{w}
note: Song lyrics (Urnade). Kept the two-line-per-page layout with \n. [JP]/[JP] rendered 'the first/second friend' without a possessive (the lyric does not say whose). [JP] singular/plural unknown; 'a sleeping face'.
Page 7: the party reports what the goblin said (relayed; not shown). [JP] kept as 'bad news' twice, mirroring the repetition.

en: "Sorry. I promised I'd sing for you as thanks, and it ended up being a one-time-only thing."{w}
"...Don't tell Volms or Mister Rondel about this, okay? You know why, right?"{w}{p}"Welp, in that case, guess I'll go looking for a new song!"{w}
note: [JP]: Haleorat's casual address for Rondelgius (shortened name + [JP]). Rendered 'Mister Rondel' (a 'the master' reading does not fit). Reason implied: Volms would be shaken by the lyrics' implication.

en:
"Your journey sure sounds like fun!"{w}{p}"...Someday,
would you let me turn your adventures into a song?{w}I bet it'd make a great song!!"{w}

note: Volms to a human party member: kept the drawn-out, sneering delivery at full force. [JP] -> ~.

en:
"My main residence
is not here in Isfald."{w}{p}"Isfald is a beautiful place, surrounded by greenery and water.{w}But it is also rather humid, you see.
It damages antiquities."{w}{p}"That is why I moved my residence somewhere drier.{w}...What? I need only have moved the storehouse?{w}You do not understand, adventurer."{w}{p}"My great pleasure is to savor the finest wine
surrounded by the works of art I have collected."{w}{p}"That, I simply cannot give up!"{w}
note: The storehouse remark is the party's (unshown) reply, echoed by Volms.

en:
"Adventurers and traveling merchants
sometimes bring the most astonishing articles."{w}{p}"For one like me, long bored of the town's antique shops,
nothing is more delightful than their visits."{w}{p}"That is why
I wish to support their journeys.{w}I shall support you as well."{w}
You received 1,000 GP!{w}

"Should you find anything rare,
do bring it to me!!"{w}
"Hmmm...{w}You there, take a look at this painting."{w}

"This, I am told, is called the Forsaken Painting 'Morning of Ruin'. Have you ever heard the name anywhere?"{w}{p}"I acquired it from a traveling merchant, but it seems the painting has passed from hand to hand, and no one any longer knows its particulars."{w}{p}"I cannot stop thinking about this painting.{w}The one depicted in it is most likely the Earth Goddess.
There can be no mistake that it is Lady Fiona."{w}{p}"Going by its title, this painting must show Lady Fiona
bidding farewell to every living thing
before the destruction of the land."{w}
note: [JP] (new term, not in glossary): 'Forsaken Painting'. [JP] (new): 'Morning of Ruin'. [JP] -> single quotes. Also appears as item names in EL_SAI/EVENT_TEXT/eboot (untranslated), so the pair should go to the glossary.

en:
"And yet Lady Fiona's land,
that is, Finas Rade,
exists, as you can see."{w}{p}"If this painting depicted past history,
would you not agree that it makes no sense?"{w}{p}"My own guess is that it is a prophetic painting,
depicting a tragedy of the land yet to come..."{w}

"If you learn anything about this painting,
come and inform me. I am counting on you."{w}{p}"Oh yes, one more thing.{w}You must not stir up fear among the people over this painting."{w}
"Not a word of this to anyone. Understood?"{w}
note: [JP] (sic for [JP]) = tell no one.

en: "Have you learned anything about the Forsaken Painting?"{w}

"Wh...{w}The true Earth Goddess...!?{w}And her name is Lady Urna...?"{w}{p}"Which means..."{w}{p}"We were originally a race raised on Lady Urna's land,
and that land was...
was nearly destroyed by the g-gods..."{w}{p}"And to save us,
Lady Urna cast herself away and fused
with the land that is now Lady Fiona's!?"{w}{p}"Then the ancient evil spirit
in Bistel's Decree... surely it isn't..."{w}{p}"O... ooohhh...!!{w}What a cruel twist of fate..."{w}{p}"Should I keep this locked away in my heart,
or else...{w}No, I shall tell the king."{w}{p}"You have done well to look into this."{w}
note: [JP]: number unmarked; 'the g-gods' chosen (stammer kept from [JP]). Could be 'a god'. [JP] = Decree per convention (no quote marks: source has none here). Urna 'her': goddess, female per glossary.

en: You received 50,000 GP!{w}
"You have my gratitude. Thank you."{w}

"Come again if you have another interesting gift for me.{w}...However,
next time, bring me something a little easier to handle, would you?"{w}
Lunea

"Yay! A customer!
Welcome, welcome!{w}This is Lunea's Shop!"{w}
"But right now there's nothing here.{w}We're all empty-dempty~"{w}
note: [JP] = playful [JP] (completely empty); rendered as a cutesy rhyme. ♪ -> ~.

en: "Hauuu... What do I dooo..."{w}

note: Lunea speaks of herself in the third person; kept. [JP] = 'weird kid' (gender-neutral; this is Caron).

en: "Coming in~!{w}At last, I've infiltrated a shop in Isfald!!{w}Wait, what is this place... It STINKS!?"{w}
note: ??? = Caron (named in 4362).

en: "Welcome!{w}Welcome to Lunea's Shop!!"{w}

"Aren't those monster tentacles!?{w}And over there, fangs and furs and... You're selling these?
Where do you even get stuff like this?"{w}

"'Stuff like this'...?{w}Uh, um, I wouldn't really call it stocking...
I just pick them up, you know, in places like Nerid...?"{w}
"You PICKED them up!?"{w}
"Y-yeah..."{w}
"Picked 'em up."{w}
"You don't have to say it twice!!"{w}
"S-sorry...{w}...Wait, why am I getting yelled at...???"{w}

"Selling customers stuff you picked up --
are you even serious about running a business!?"{w}

"Huh? But..."{w}{p}"Alchemists and the like,
there are people who buy them every now and then, you know?{w}I don't think there's anything strange about it..."{w}
"Oh, I get it!"{w}
"So you understand~!"{w}
"No, that's not what I meant.{w}There are other shops in Isfald, right?{w}Proper ones!"{w}
"...I like to think this one's proper too, though..."{w}
"Soooo... where might the other shops be, hmm?"{w}
note: Caron forcing a sweet tone over irritation (see 4348).

en:
"Uuu,
the irritation peeking out from behind that smile is scary..."{w}
"The only shop worth calling a shop is Lunea's Shop, you know?{w}Oh, do you mean everyday goods, or a place to eat!?{w}For those, there's a really good place..."{w}

note: [JP]♪ -> 'Non, non~'.

en:
"Oh, then this year
the Paralysis Fangs are selling really well!{w}The secret is in this sharp tip... Ow!?"{w}
note: [JP] = item (ITEM.CSV:540), new term 'Paralysis Fang'; item name not yet translated elsewhere.

en: "I-I'm g-g-g-g-going numb..."{w}
note: [JP]: stutter of [JP] (paralysis).

en: "Wh-- what are you doing!?{w}Are you an idiot or something!?"{w}
"Hngggggggggg..."{w}
note: [JP]: paralysed gurgle, rendered as an English noise rather than romanized.
[JP]: gender unknown, so 'That kid' (echoes [JP] in 4312) instead of a pronoun.

en: "I picked up a Tentacles tentacle...{w}I was going to put it up for sale, but...{w}I got hungry... and ate it."{w}
note: [JP] = monster (MONSTER1.CSV:6/7), new name 'Tentacles' (untranslated elsewhere). 'a Tentacles tentacle' keeps the joke of the source.

en: "Empty-dempty all over again...{w}What am I really gonna dooo..."{w}
note: [JP] again, same rendering as 4308.

en:
Nobody is here.{w}Some sort of note has been left on the desk.{w}{p}"Welcome to Lunea's shop!{w}Lunea is away from the shop for a little while, restocking.{w}Destination: the usual, the Nerid Marshlands."{w}{p}"If I'm not back by tomorrow,
somebody please come rescue me."{w}{p}The note is dated three days ago...{w}
note: Note text in [JP] rendered with double quotes (quoted writing, not a title). [JP] read as [JP] (be away).

en:
"Whew, that was a real ordeal!{w}But thanks to it, I got to be friends with all of you,
so not everything in this world is bad!"{w}
"Maybe I should hold off on adventuring for a while..."{w}

"Oh, I know! Let me buy any items you don't need, right here!"{w}{p}"I can only buy and sell for 0 GP, but when the moment comes,
I'll hand them right back to you!"{w}
"...Can you even call that buying?{w}It's more like a storage shed... Huh???"{w}
"Oh well!{w}Everyone, please keep coming back to Lunea's Shop~!"{w}
{0E}        *   0 GP Shop Unlocked   *        {0F}{w}
note: Centered banner: full-width spaces replaced with ASCII spaces; centering approximate, check in game. Term '0 GP Shop' (new; HELP_TEXT uses [JP]).

en:
"Actually, you see,
I've been writing letters with Caron ever since."{w}{p}"And guess what? Caron...{w}is running a shop in Semnadoc!"{w}{p}"We've become really good friends now,
and Caron's been teaching me the ins and outs of doing business."{w}{p}"Apparently Caron
even has a brand named after Caron!{w}Amazing, isn't it!!"{w}{p}"I bet there's all sorts of stuff, like Caron Fangs and Caron Furs!{w}You should definitely go check it out too, customer!"{w}
note: Caron's gender unknown: name repeated instead of a pronoun ([JP] -> 'a brand named after Caron'). Glossary has 'Caron brand'. 'Caron Fangs/Furs' are Lunea's guesses, not real items.

en:
Oldaim, the residence of the Isfald royal family,
is open to audiences even for commoners,
by the king's wish to close the distance to the people.{w}{p}Thanks to that, you were able to get inside
with surprising ease.{w}{p}However, once shown into the audience chamber,
you realized you had no 'reason for an audience',
the one thing that mattered.{w}
note: [JP] -> single quotes (set-off phrase).

en: Guard
"Now then, what is your business here?"{w}

Before the audience, the guard asked your business,
but you could not give any answer.{w}
"What? You wish to see the king with no business at all!?{w}The audience chamber is a precious place where the people and the king meet.{w}We cannot have you coming here to gawk like sightseers!"{w}

Just as the guard was about to throw you out,
a girl happened to pass by.{w}
"What a racket. Is there some sort of quarrel?"{w}
note: ??? = Leafa (named in 4401).

en:
"My apologies, Lady Leafa.{w}These people wandered into the castle half in jest,
so I was about to send them away."{w}
note: [JP] from the guard = 'Lady Leafa'; [JP] in 4405 = 'Princess'.

en: Leafa
"Hmm. You have quite some nerve, don't you?{w}I like that. Come over here a moment."{w}
note: Addressed to the party (nerve = barging into an audience with no business).

en: "Princess, what do you intend to do!?"{w}

"Well, I'm bored.{w}I thought I might ask them a small favor."{w}{p}"...I shall tell you this up front:
should you get any strange ideas,
not only Isfald's soldiers..."{w}{p}"...but the whole nation, its people included,
will be your enemy,
so bear that in mind."{w}
note: Page 1 answers the guard (so 'them' = the party); pages 2-3 turn to the party. Sentence cut across pages kept at the source's point.
